findings.issue: The three converted callers (lv_call, gs_gate, _cli_here) call run_script_in_process with no process fallback, and the runner now raises ValueError when the environment's PYTHONPATH holds a sitecustomize. reach-diff puts one there by design. When the interpreter's user site is off (-s, PYTHONNOUSERSITE, or any venv without system site packages), it writes its hook as sitecustomize rather than usercustomize (tools/reach-diff.py:41-44, 55-57, 767). Under it every in-process fb, at4 and at6 call in test_audit_task raises, because _cli_here and lv_env copy os.environ (PYTHONPATH included) and gs_gate inherits it. The suite is then green at base HEAD (processes) and red at WORKTREE, so this task's own declared gate `reach-diff.py ... --head WORKTREE` cannot pass on such an interpreter. test_drive_phase avoids this only because it routes through _needs_process before calling the runner. The PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE sentence 'it refuses an env planting a sitecustomize ... so a case whose subject is the process boundary still starts one' is false for these callers: nothing starts a process, the case raises.
findings.resolution: Route the way the drive suite does. In _cli_here, lv_call and gs_gate, when `_harness.planted_sitecustomize(env or os.environ)` returns a path, run the old subprocess.run form (the code this diff replaced) and return the same shape. Alternatively, give run_script_in_process an opt-in that runs `subprocess.run([sys.executable, path] + args, ...)` with the same (code, out, err) return when a sitecustomize is planted, and keep the bare refusal as the default. Add a case that points PYTHONPATH at a directory holding a sitecustomize.py and asserts _cli_here still answers fb5's refusal. Reword the guide's 'still starts one' to say what the caller must do.

findings.issue: The runner replaces only the sys.stdin, sys.stdout and sys.stderr objects. A child process the script starts without its own pipes inherits this suite's file descriptors 0, 1 and 2, not the byte-backed streams. That child's output is missing from the returned bytes and goes to the suite's own stdout or stderr. A case asserting that a script printed nothing on stderr therefore passes in-process and fails as a process: the silent-pass shape. The docstring promises 'the way subprocess.run would run it as a process', and the WHAT IT CANNOT BE block does not name this. No converted verb reaches it today: audit-task.py's spawns at :3751, :5539, :6570, :14598 and :15101 all pipe, and run-test-gate.py:3145 spawns through _spawn_kwargs. But the helper is now offered to every suite under tests/.
findings.resolution: Add to the WHAT IT CANNOT BE block that a child the script starts with inherited stdio writes to this suite's descriptors, so its output is not in the returned bytes. A case whose subject includes a child's inherited output runs as a process. If it should be enforced instead, os.dup2 descriptors 1 and 2 onto temporary files for the duration of the run and append their contents.

findings.issue: The guide names the signature as `run_script_in_process(path, args, cwd, stdin, env)` and leaves out `before_main`. The task description names that parameter, test_drive_phase._run_in_process depends on it (tests/test_drive_phase.py:368-370 passes _route_verbs), and ip11 proves it. A reader of the guide looking for how a script's own function is rerouted before its __main__ runs will not find it.
findings.resolution: Write the signature as `run_script_in_process(path, args, cwd, stdin, env, before_main)` and add one clause: before_main(namespace) runs between the script's body and its __main__ block, for a caller that reroutes what the command line will call.
